name: 1801-1935 Indiana Avenue — the east frontage, 18th to 20th Street, as a background row (district draft; refined by T-3145)
aka: Indiana Avenue's east frontage, 18th to 20th Street

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The 1904 Blue Book (published 1903, for 1904) puts households on the face at the target; the phase keeps the study's 1904-1911 window (study ruling 11), and its 1911 end is that window, not a sighting.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body (u -26.020, v -13.640 m from the building's front and southernmost faces), set from the corner at local (1278.47, -3462.15): Indiana Avenue's east line as the 1904 grid carries it between sheets 20 and 35 (data/street_grid/1904.json, ruling: carried straight), with its centre 10.06 m (66 ft) west of it; the row runs from 1.0 m inside 20th Street's measured north line to 1.0 m inside 18th Street's south line, and each house's front stands behind the street line by its model's own drafted setback. Good to the georeference and a lot either way. Rotation 179.356 degrees squares the plan to the avenue.
placement.symbolic_location: The east frontage of Indiana Avenue from 18th to 20th Street, the Indiana half of the block whose Prairie half holds Glessner, Kimball and Keith: on Sanborn 1911 sheet 27, which is not in hand.

footprint.note: The row's outline, along every house's front and back: a background mass, so the side yards inside it are not walkable ground.

stories.note: Three storeys, the commonest count among the neighbouring drafts (15 of 23); each house's own count is its model's, in the plan.

construction.note: Brick, as 18 of the 23 neighbouring Indiana drafts are on their sheets (three of them with stone fronts; the other five are frame); nothing in hand says what this face was built of.

draft_plan.note: The face splits at the half-block where the same block's Prairie face turns from 1834 to 1900 (122.3 m): the 1800s half, where the Blue Book lists a run of consecutive odd numbers (1813-1833, each a separate household), is a row of the 20th-21st face's 3B houses (2007-2027, its consecutive numbers on lots of about 8 m), and the 1900s half, where it lists three households in 122 m (1901, 1921, 1933), is the 16th-18th face's freestanding houses (1601-1703). Each house is its model's drafted main body at its model's setback, centred on its model's lot width stretched by one factor per half so the lots meet the corners; rear ranges, porches and stables are not carried. A Blue Book number is placed at about 2.9 m per number south of 18th Street in the 1800s and 3.5 m per number from the half-block in the 1900s, as the Prairie face of this block prints them (1834 ends 116.7 m, 1900 begins 123.5 m, 1936 ends 245 m), and each house's row of the plan names the numbers that fall on it.

draft.note: The draft's own provenance: the pass that wrote it, the rows it read and the tickets that replace it attribute by attribute under this id.

function.note: Dwellings: the 1904 Blue Book (the street-and-number list's Indiana Avenue section, about printed page 156; the item's OCR text, lines 24563-24597) seats households at ten numbers on this face, 1813, 1815, 1819, 1821, 1825, 1829 and 1833 in the 1800s and 1901, 1921 and 1933 in the 1900s, so houses stood along it at the target. The Blue Book lists selected households only, so a number it omits is not thereby empty, and it says nothing of the buildings themselves.

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-3011, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-3145 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the rules' site row (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-district-background-3011). Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 27, the sheet that draws this face, is not among the committed scans (data/street_grid/1904.json carries Indiana's east line straight between sheets 20 and 35 and leaves the face unlotted), and the visibility census (data/components/prairie_1904/background_census.json) finds the ground seen from 48 Prairie stands, the most-seen target behind the avenue. So the face is drafted as ONE BACKGROUND ROW rather than left bare: 22 houses whose presence the Blue Book's ten households carry and whose every dimension is re-stood from the drafted houses of the neighbouring Indiana faces (the 16th-18th face off sheet 20, the 20th-21st face off sheet 35). T-3145 ingests sheet 27 and replaces the row house by house.
